channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Decreased Prices for Certain Food Products
item.description: Kazakhstan's food inflation has slowed for the second consecutive month, with a deflationary trend of 0.1%. Prices for sugar, onions, apples, carrots, and lamb decreased last week, while bread, pasta, butter, salt, and tea prices remained stable.

item.title: New Comfort-Class Building in Shchuchinsk Lacks Adequate Heating, Residents Complain
item.description: Residents of a newly constructed comfort-class apartment building in Shchuchinsk, Akmola region, are struggling with insufficient heating despite the official start of the heating season. Radiators remain cold, forcing residents to use electric heaters to maintain a minimum temperature of 18 degrees Celsius, incurring additional costs.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Addresses Land Grabbing Allegations in Bazar-Korgon
item.description: Member of Parliament Aybek Altynbekov has responded to accusations of illegally using land and seizing a market in the Bazar-Korgon district. He stated that disputes should be resolved based on documents and law, not personal opinions. President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into the land use.

item.title: Trump Considered 200% Tariffs on Ukraine and Russia to End Conflict
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated he considered imposing 200% tariffs on Ukraine and Russia if they did not reach a peace agreement. He claimed this tactic helped end five wars but expressed doubt about its effectiveness in this specific case due to limited US trade with both nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Ukraine Sign Memorandum on Cooperation in Pharmaceutical Regulation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Ukraine have signed a memorandum of cooperation in pharmaceutical regulation. A Ukrainian delegation visited Tashkent to discuss experiences in developing healthcare systems, drug reimbursement mechanisms, and ensuring affordable medicines. The agreement aims to facilitate Ukrainian drug exports to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Central Asia's Heritage Presented at the UN in Geneva
item.description: Uzbekistan's Center for Islamic Civilization showcased the region's scientific and spiritual heritage at an international exhibition and conference in Geneva. The event brought together diplomats, international organization representatives, scholars, and cultural figures to discuss new scientific and educational projects. It highlighted the contributions of scholars from Bukhara, Samarkand, and Termez to world civilization.

item.title: Akyin Askat Zhetigen Announces Entry into Politics
item.description: Renowned akyin Askat Zhetigen has declared his intention to enter politics, stating his commitment to realizing his political views constructively. He plans to continue his cultural work, promoting Kyrgyz history, traditional music, and art internationally. Zhetigen previously faced charges related to public calls for riots and power seizure.

item.title: Ten Astana Residents to Stand Trial for Illegal Driver's License Issuance
item.description: An organized criminal group involved in the illegal issuance of driver's licenses has been investigated in Astana. The group, consisting of special public service center employees and facilitators, allegedly issued 74 licenses illegally in 2025. The case, involving charges of creating and leading a criminal group and information manipulation, has been sent to court.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Replace Official Cars with Electric Vehicles
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's government vehicles are slated for a gradual replacement with electric cars, as announced by President Sadyr Japarov. The initiative is part of a broader plan to establish domestic electric vehicle assembly, with a factory expected to launch by late 2026 or early 2027. This move aims to phase out older gasoline and diesel vehicles.

item.title: Russia's Central Bank Head Calls for Limiting Preferential Mortgages
item.description: The head of Russia's Central Bank has urged for restrictions on preferential mortgage programs. This call comes amid concerns about the potential overheating of the housing market and the sustainability of such subsidized lending schemes. The specific measures proposed were not detailed in the initial report.

item.title: Tajikistan's Economy Minister Inspects Panj Free Economic Zone
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade, Abdurahmonzoda Abdurahmon Safarali, visited the Panj Free Economic Zone (SEZ). The visit aimed to fulfill President Emomali Rahmon's directives on establishing industrial enterprises. The minister reviewed SEZ conditions, construction progress, and landscaping efforts.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Journalist Batyrbekov arrested for two months in criminal case
item.description: Journalist Amangeldy Batyrbekov has been detained for two months in a criminal case, following a 20-day administrative arrest. The Saryagash District Court ordered his pre-trial detention. The arrest is reportedly linked to his videos about activist Kural Seyithanuly. Batyrbekov was previously sentenced to 20 days for defamation.

item.title: Two oil supertankers severely damaged by mine explosions in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two oil supertankers, with a combined capacity exceeding 4.5 million barrels, were severely damaged by mine explosions while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The ships' engine rooms sustained heavy damage, leaving them immobile. Iranian state television broadcast footage of the damaged tankers. This follows a similar incident on October 17.

item.title: First Human Death Recorded from Chamond Virus in France
item.description: France has recorded its first human death attributed to the Chamond virus, previously only found in animals. The patient, who had severe immunodeficiency, died on October 22nd in Lyon after experiencing neurological complications. The virus is suspected to have been transmitted by an insect bite.

item.title: First Flight Carries 140 Passengers from Kazakhstan to Oman
item.description: Air Astana launched a new international flight route from Astana to Salalah, Oman, on October 24th. The inaugural flight carried 140 passengers, filling all seats. This route aims to develop aviation and expand transit opportunities, fulfilling a presidential directive.

item.title: Kazakhstan Health Ministry Addresses Rumors of New COVID-19 Strain 'Stratus'
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has stated that the epidemiological situation regarding COVID-19 remains stable. The 'Stratus' variant (XFG lineage of Omicron) is not new and has been circulating for some time. The ministry reported a significant decrease in COVID-19 cases compared to the previous year and assured that current variants pose no additional risks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Poet and Activist Askat Jetigen Announces Entry into Politics
item.description: Askat Jetigen, a poet and civil activist from Kyrgyzstan, recently released after three years in prison, has announced his entry into politics. He stated on Facebook that he will focus on developing culture, history, and traditional Kyrgyz music, maintaining his previous political stance.

item.title: Taliban Denies Funding Insecurity in Pakistan, Cites Lack of Resources
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid rejected Pakistani allegations of fueling insecurity, stating Afghanistan lacks resources for such actions. He argued that instability in Pakistan harms Afghanistan and the region. Mujahid suggested Pakistani security institutions are deflecting blame for their inability to maintain domestic security.

item.title: Kazakh Journalist Amangeldy Batyrbekov Detained for Two Months on Defamation Charges
item.description: Journalist Amangeldy Batyrbekov has been detained for two months following a 20-day administrative arrest. A court in Saragash district ordered his detention on criminal charges on October 22nd. Batyrbekov, chief editor of "Saragash-Inform," was previously fined for defamation and had his detention extended, reportedly linked to his reporting on activist Kural Seitkhanuly.

item.title: CSTO Special Forces Exercise 'Cobalt-2026' Concludes in Tajikistan
item.description: The special exercise 'Cobalt-2026' involving special forces units of the CSTO Collective Rapid Deployment Force concluded in Tajikistan on October 23, 2026. The drills, held from October 18-23 at the 'Magob' training ground, focused on combating illegal armed groups, paramilitary drug trafficking groups, and hostage rescue. Participants honed skills in simulated combat conditions, incorporating lessons from recent military operations.

item.title: US Secretly Recalling Diplomats from Middle East Embassies, CNN Reports
item.description: The United States is reportedly recalling diplomats from several Middle East countries, including Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Lebanon. The State Department confirmed temporary staff adjustments at US embassies in Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar, and Jordan. The exact reasons for these recall measures remain undisclosed.

item.title: Karazhal Development Accelerates in Ulytau Region
item.description: In the four years since Ulytau Region's establishment, significant development has been observed in Karazhal city and Zheyrem settlement's industrial, infrastructural, and social sectors. Industrial output is projected to reach 198 billion tenge in the first nine months of this year, a 44.7% increase from last year. Investment in fixed capital is expected to total 66 billion tenge.

item.title: France Deploys 70,000 Police and Special Units for Upcoming Demonstrations
item.description: France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has announced an enhanced security plan for anticipated demonstrations on October 24th. Approximately 70,000 police and gendarmerie officers will be mobilized, an increase from previous protests. Special units, armored vehicles, and water cannons will be deployed to maintain order and prevent violence and looting.

item.title: Astana Investigation Concludes on Illegal Driver's License Issuance; Six Suspects Arrested
item.description: An investigation into the illegal issuance of driver's licenses in Astana has concluded, with six suspects arrested. The scheme involved special service center employees and intermediaries who facilitated the fraudulent acquisition of licenses for 74 individuals in 2025. The case has been sent to court.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Oman Launch Direct Flights Connecting Astana and Almaty to Salalah
item.description: Direct flights have commenced between Kazakhstan and Oman, with Air Astana launching a new route from Astana to Salalah. The first flight carried 140 passengers. Another flight from Almaty to Salalah also had full capacity. SalamAir also operates a route from Almaty to Muscat, fostering tourism and economic ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Introducing Islamic Finance 'Murabaha' Standard
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has proposed introducing the Islamic finance 'Murabaha' standard. This would allow banks to sell goods to customers on credit, clearly stating the purchase price and markup. The standard prohibits additional markups for delayed payments.

item.title: Kazakhstan Played Key Role in Establishing C5+1 Cooperation Format with USA
item.description: Kazakhstan was instrumental in creating the C5+1 format, which unites Central Asian nations and the US for dialogue on economy, trade, security, and technology. The idea for a direct dialogue platform was discussed before the official launch. Kazakhstan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Kairat Umarov, shared details of its inception.

item.title: Astana Investigation Uncovers Scheme for Illegal Driver's Licenses
item.description: An investigation in Astana has concluded into an organized criminal group involved in illegally obtaining driver's licenses. The group included employees of the Specialized Public Service Center and intermediaries. 74 individuals acquired licenses through this illicit scheme, and their documents have now been invalidated.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Envoy Warns of Growing Religious Freedom Restrictions Under Taliban
item.description: Afghanistan's UN envoy, Naseer Ahmad Faieq, stated that religious freedom faces increasing restrictions under Taliban rule. He highlighted discrimination against religious minorities, particularly Shia Muslims, and concerns over the Taliban's use of religious interpretations to justify policies against women and girls. Faieq emphasized that these actions contradict Islamic principles.

item.title: New Islands Emerge in Caspian Sea, Scientists Warn of Aral Sea's Fate
item.description: New islands are continuously appearing in the northern Caspian Sea off the coast of Kazakhstan, some reaching a kilometer in length. Wild animals have been spotted on the newly exposed land. However, scientists warn that this phenomenon is linked to the ongoing decline of the Caspian Sea's water level, which could have severe consequences for the region's ecosystem, potentially mirroring the Aral Sea disaster.

item.title: Kazakhstan Teachers' Salaries Vary Significantly by Region, Almaty Region Reports Highest Pay.
item.description: Teachers' salaries in Kazakhstan show significant regional disparities, with the lowest monthly pay at 33,497 tenge and the highest reaching 1.2 million tenge in the Almaty region. Factors influencing salary include qualifications, teaching load, and additional responsibilities like class supervision.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Finance Ministry to Gain New Budgetary Control Powers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance will have expanded powers in managing state funds, debt, and controlling budget expenditures. A new government resolution grants the ministry authority to develop financial instruments, assess investment project efficiency, and manage the Stabilization Fund. It will also establish a digital system for auditing state finances and reporting corruption.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes First Industrial Park in Chuy Region for Public Discussion
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce has proposed the creation of the country's first industrial park in the Chuy region, covering over 24 hectares. The project, estimated at 1.5 billion soms, aims to attract investment, create jobs, and develop industrial infrastructure. The managing company will be state-owned, with plans to transition to self-financing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ranks Fifth Globally in Projected Economic Growth for 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is projected to rank fifth globally in economic growth for 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund's forecasts. The country's economy is expected to grow significantly, with Guyana and Taiwan leading the projected growth rates. This forecast was shared by Temir Sariev, President of the Chamber of Commerce and former Prime Minister.

item.title: Astana Police Dismantle Criminal Group Issuing Illegal Driving Licenses
item.description: Astana authorities have concluded an investigation into an organized crime group involved in the illegal issuance of driving licenses. The group, comprising Special Public Service Center employees and intermediaries, facilitated cheating on theory tests and falsifying practical exam results. 74 individuals obtained licenses fraudulently in 2025.

item.title: Oil Prices Hit Five-Month High, Raising Inflation Concerns for Kazakhstan
item.description: Oil prices have reached their highest level in five months, with Brent crude exceeding $114 per barrel, driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East. Experts predict this could increase budget revenues but also fuel global inflation, potentially raising import costs for Kazakhstan. The long-term impact on the global economy is viewed negatively.

item.title: US Reportedly Proposes Ukraine Join EU in Exchange for NATO Renunciation
item.description: The United States is reportedly proposing that Ukraine join the European Union in exchange for renouncing NATO membership, according to The Economist. The US peace plan also includes easing sanctions on Russia, partially restoring its relations with the West, and establishing a demilitarized zone in the Donetsk region.

item.title: Early Marriages in Tajikistan: UNICEF Highlights Persistent Issue and Solutions
item.description: An estimated 5,600 marriages involving girls under 18 occur annually in Tajikistan. In 2024, courts approved 3,804 requests to lower the marriage age, with 771 marriages officially registered for 17-year-old girls. UNICEF supports research highlighting the social and behavioral factors contributing to child marriages.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Awards Internal Affairs Ministry Staff for Service
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has awarded a group of employees from the Ministry of Internal Affairs for their long-term service, contributions to public safety, and exemplary work. Awards included the orders of 'Mehnat shuhrati', 'Mardlik', 'Do'stlik', and 'Salomatlik II degree', as well as the 'Jasorat' medal.

item.title: Uzbekistan Cracks Down on Illegal Sales of Liquefied Gas Cylinders
item.description: Over 120 cases of illegal liquefied gas cylinder circulation were detected in Uzbekistan between October 19-21. Authorities confiscated over 3,000 cylinders, totaling 13.6 tons, intended for un-gassified areas. The crackdown involved security services, the Interior Ministry, and the Prosecutor General's Office.
